title: Gideon and the Echo
premise: Ines Halloran, an insurance investigator who has spent twelve years cataloging impossible accidents in contested orbits, is assigned to the Erebus, a deep-space hauler that returned with its crew aged backward and its logs rewritten. Her investigation uncovers that the ship's jump drive folded time around a stolen alien artifact—and that the two rival fleets blockading the station will go to war over it unless someone maintains the fiction that the artifact never existed. Ines must keep the lie alive long enough for the next jump window to open, then choose between erasing her own memories of the truth or letting the fleets destroy each other. She sacrifices her recollections of the twelve years she spent finding belonging among spacers, preserving peace at the cost of the only home she ever had.
about_author: Bram Vasquez is a former maritime insurance adjuster who traded harbor paperwork for starfield speculation after a decade of investigating losses no one could explain. He writes from a converted tugboat, where he insists the rocking helps him hear how stories want to be told.

chapters.title: Actuarial Grace
chapters.summary: Ines Halloran, POV. Ines arrives at Meridian Station to investigate the Erebus's impossible return: thirty crew members now biologically younger than their service records. The emotional beat is professional detachment cracking into unease as she interviews a captain who remembers a daughter he hasn't yet had.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Loss
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Cross-referencing cargo manifests, Ines finds a forty-ton discrepancy hidden inside a routine ore shipment—the space where something was carried out and brought back wrong. Fleet auditors begin shadowing her. The beat is mounting dread as she realizes both blockading fleets already know more than they admit.

chapters.title: Younger Every Hour
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Chief Engineer Okafor, one of the de-aged crew. Okafor experiences memories arriving out of order—grieving events that haven't happened. Ines bonds with him over shared rootlessness. The beat is tenderness blooming in an investigation that should stay cold.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Window
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Summoned by both fleet commands simultaneously, Ines learns each side believes the other stole an alien artifact called the Echo. A mediator proposes a joint inquiry; Ines sees it collapse into posturing. The beat is claustrophobic politics as the jump window countdown begins.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Okafor, POV. Okafor's fragmenting memories reveal the truth: the crew found the Echo drifting in deep space, and their first jump attempt folded the ship through its own timeline. The beat is horror and awe as he realizes the artifact doesn't store memory—it devours it.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Ines fabricates evidence that the Echo was destroyed on approach, buying the fleets a fragile truce. But a young fleet analyst catches the forgery and blackmails her. The beat is moral vertigo—she's become the kind of investigator she spent twelve years hunting.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Cargo
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Cornered by the analyst and running out of window, Ines traces the Echo's origin to a derelict near the station where she first found belonging among spacers. Flashbacks braid her past with the present crisis. The beat is grief for a life built from small, unrecorded kindnesses.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The analyst exposes the lie; both fleets mobilize as the final jump window opens. Okafor, half-erased, offers to carry the Echo back into the fold himself. The beat is desperate momentum—every character choosing what they can't afford to lose.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, climax. Ines takes the Echo to the derelict herself, using the drive to fold the artifact out of reachable space—but the fold demands equivalent memory as payment. She feeds it her twelve years among the spacers, the only home she ever made. The beat is sacrifice rendered in real time.

chapters.title: Echo
chapters.summary: Ines, POV, resolution. The fleets stand down, believing the artifact never existed; the lie holds because only Ines could have disproven it, and she no longer knows it was a lie. Okafor greets her like a stranger who feels familiar. The beat is bittersweet belonging—she has no memory of home, but home remembers her.
